comparisons.peer_topic: Carrying value and cumulative hedging adjustments for interest rate hedges
comparisons.peer_summary: The carrying values of investments, deposits, and unsecured borrowings designated in interest rate hedging relationships include cumulative hedging adjustments, which were $(5.81) billion as of December 2024 and $(5.63) billion as of December 2023, largely related to de-designated unsecured long-term borrowings. The amortized cost of investments was $35.29 billion as of December 2024 and $17.33 billion as of December 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS disclose the impact of de-designated hedging relationships on the carrying values of debt securities and borrowings. BAC reports that fair value adjustments from de-designated long-term debt and AFS debt securities hedges decreased their respective carrying values by $11.2 billion and $4.4 billion as of December 31, 2024. Similarly, GS reports cumulative hedging adjustments from prior hedging relationships that were de-designated (mostly unsecured long-term borrowings) included in carrying values, amounting to a decrease of $(5.81) billion as of December 2024. Both companies reflect the amortization or inclusion of these adjustments in the carrying value of the associated liabilities/assets after de-designation.

sentences.text: At December 31, 2024 and 2023, the fair value adjustments from de-designated long-term debt hedges decreased the long-term debt carrying value by $11.2 billion and $10.5 billion.
The fair value adjustments from de-designated AFS debt securities hedges decreased the AFS debt securities carrying value by $4.4 billion and $5.6 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023.
The fair value adjustments are being amortized or accreted into interest over the contractual lives of the assets or liabilities.

• Cumulative hedging adjustment included $(5.81) billion as of December 2024 and $(5.63) billion as of December 2023 of hedging adjustments from prior hedging relationships that were de-designated and substantially all were related to unsecured long-term borrowings.

comparisons.peer_topic: Basis adjustments for de-designated hedged items
comparisons.peer_summary: Certain basis adjustments exist on the balance sheet date associated with hedged items that have been de-designated from qualifying fair value hedging relationships.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address basis adjustments resulting from de-designated fair value hedges. BAC explicitly states that fair value adjustments from de-designated hedges decreased carrying values and are being amortized or accreted into interest over the contractual lives. JPM's footnote in its long-term debt schedule identifies basis adjustments existing on the balance sheet date associated with hedged items that have been de-designated from qualifying fair value hedging relationships, indicating a shared accounting mechanism for tracking the residual hedge ineffectiveness or fair value changes after a relationship ceases to be designated.

comparisons.peer_topic: Hedge De-designation Accounting and Portfolio Layer Method
comparisons.peer_summary: Upon de-designation, basis adjustments are amortized to interest income/expense over the remaining life. For certain AFS securities, the portfolio layer method allows hedging of prepayable and non-prepayable assets at the portfolio level with basis adjustments maintained until de-designation events, with the hedged amount being the sum of notional amounts of outstanding layers.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures describe the accounting treatment of basis adjustments upon de-designation of fair value hedges. BAC notes that fair value adjustments from de-designated hedges are amortized or accreted into interest over the contractual lives. MS specifies that when a derivative is de-designated, any remaining basis adjustment is amortized to Interest income (expense) over the remaining life using the effective interest method. Both companies align in amortizing the residual fair value impact into earnings over the life of the instrument.

sentences.text: The fair value adjustments are being amortized or accreted into interest over the contractual lives of the assets or liabilities.

When a derivative is de-designated as a hedge, any basis adjustment remaining on the hedged asset (liability) is amortized to Interest income (expense) over the remaining life of the asset (liability) using the effective interest method.
